extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of natural philosophy / evolutionary theory (educated general readers and scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and characterizing the distinctive traits or criteria by which the author defines and illustrates 'Evolution' across physical, biological, social, and cognitive domains. The page presents general propositions and examples that serve as standards for recognising evolutionary change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase in definiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: An essential characteristic of advancing Science is increase in definiteness — a change from vague, fluctuating, and indefinite use of terms and relations to limited, precise, and definite knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained as a universal trait of progress: mathematics (Euclid arranging propositions), mechanics (clearer concepts like inertia and forces), astronomy (timing of celestial phenomena improving from errors of days to seconds). The author emphasizes that terms and relations originally used vaguely become progressively limited and precise. Examples across arts, industry, and sciences illustrate how representation and manufacture become more exact with social and technical advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress from qualitative to quantitative
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution manifests as a transition from qualitative statements that certain phenomena are associated, to quantitative relations that specify how much of one accompanies how much of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reduction of vague connexions to distinct, measurable relations is exemplified in physics (mechanical, chemical, thermal laws), chemistry (constituents and combining equivalents), physiology (weighing, spirometer, sphygmograph), pathology (statistical methods), botany/zoology (numerical comparisons), and sociology (census and trade tables). Emphasizes inferential accuracy about antecedents and consequents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolution from the homogeneous to the heterogeneous
rubrics_metrics.description: A universal law: evolution is a change from an original state of homogeneity to a state of heterogeneity — differentiation and multiplication of unlike parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by many examples (arts, tools, organisms, celestial bodies). The author pairs this with the complementary law 'from the indefinite to the definite' and points out that heterogeneity arises as parts segregate and take on distinct forms and functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified formula — from indefinite incoherent homogeneity to definite coherent heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: A more specific statement: evolution is 'a change from an indefinite, incoherent homogeneity, to a definite coherent heterogeneity, accompanying the dissipation of motion and integration of matter.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates and synthesizes the preceding traits into a single formula tying together material concentration (integration of matter) and energetic change (dissipation of motion). It is presented as the author's refined definition to capture the material and dynamical aspects of evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redistribution and concentration of matter (aggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution involves passage of matter from a diffused to an aggregated state — the concentration/aggregation of dispersed units into denser, more consolidated wholes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by nebular contraction to planets, formation of continents and oceans (enabling definite air and water currents), and historical progress in industrial manufacture (from crude flint implements to precisely machined surfaces). The aggregation produces sharper boundaries and clearer part-outlines as parts draw in peripheral portions previously imperfectly disunited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redistribution and integration of retained motion (dynamical aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alongside material aggregation, retained (non-escaping) motion is redistributed: diffused, insensible molecular motions aggregate into sensible motions of masses; retained motion becomes more integrated and organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues 'concrete motion arises by the aggregation of diffused motion' and that as evolution proceeds, there is 'a decrease in the relative movements of parts and an increase in the relative movements of wholes.' Examples: genesis of planetary rotations from nebular motions, atmospheric and oceanic circulations becoming definite trade winds and currents, and biological motions (from molecular to organ-level movements). Conflicting momenta are neutralized (dissipated as heat) while outstanding integrated motions remain and become characteristic rhythms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase in multiformity and plurality of rhythms
rubrics_metrics.description: As aggregation and heterogeneity increase, the retained motions diversify into a greater variety of distinct rhythms — more kinds of periodic and compound motions arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes that 'all motion is rhythmical' and that increased variety of aggregates and their relations to forces generates new orders of rhythm. Examples include differing molecular undulations in gases, planetary revolutions and rotations producing compound perturbations and precessions, and compounded biological rhythms (circulatory, respiratory, digestive patterns). Where incident forces scale with mass (gravity) rhythms may be unaffected by aggregation, but generally new aggregation spawns new rhythms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration and specialization of functions (biological systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structures and functions become both more consolidated (integrated) and more various (specialized); general functions subdivide into distinct subordinate functions coordinated into systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed biological examples: evolution of circulatory systems from irregular nutritive movements to definite circulations with afferent/efferent distinctions; alimentary canal differentiating into mouth (prehension, mastication), oesophagus, stomach, intestines and rectum with different mechanical and secretory roles; formation of vascular, nervous controls integrating functions. As functions subdivide they also become co-ordinated and interdependent (e.g., alimentation with respiratory and circulatory systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of psychical/mental functions parallel to physiological integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Mental/psychological processes (consciousness, attention, reasoning, language) evolve in parallel with nervous and muscular integration: from homogeneous, inarticulate, uncoordinated activities to differentiated, definite, and integrated mental acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include the child's speech development: infantine noises → multiplication of sounds → articulation of consonants → terminal consonants and polysyllables; parallel intellectual development from simple recognition to deliberate induction, deduction, imagination, mathematics, music, and poetry. Attention, coherent series of impressions, and precise judgments improve with maturity as nervous processes become better coordinated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress toward precision in arts, industry, and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural and industrial products show an evolution from inexact, indeterminate forms to accurate, precise, and realistic representation and manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations: prehistoric flint tools vs modern machined surfaces; Chinese junk example for lack of straight lines; improvements from ancient furniture and locks to modern precision instruments (dividing-engine, micrometer, microscopes). In Fine Arts and literature, progress from supernatural, improbable plots and vague personages to novels and plays valued for fidelity to individual character and plausible plots.
